input.command: cat -n src/crypto.ts; ls; git ls-files | grep -iE "test|spec" ; grep -rn "crypto" --include=*.ts --include=*.js --include=*.json . 2>/dev/null | grep -v node_modules | head -30

input.reason: The claim holds. The working tree has 13 files: package.json and 12 files in src/, with no test or spec files anywhere. package.json defines "test": "node --test", but that command finds no test files, so nothing checks src/crypto.ts. Nothing tests that encrypt() output can be decrypted back to the original text (the round trip), and nothing tests that decrypt() rejects a changed ciphertext or auth tag (tamper detection). One weak point is left unchecked: decrypt() (src/crypto.ts:10-15) splits the sealed string and passes the tag to setAuthTag with no check on its length, and no authTagLength is set on createDecipheriv. A tamper test is the kind of test that would find this. Neither encrypt nor decrypt is called anywhere else in src/, so the missing tests are a quality and reliability gap, not a failure on a live code path.

evidence.location: file listing (find . -type f): no test files

input.failure_scenario: Someone changes encrypt() or decrypt() in src/crypto.ts, for example the token order or encoding, or how the auth tag is handled. Data sealed by encrypt() then no longer decrypts, or decrypt() accepts a shortened or altered auth tag. Running npm test ("node --test") still passes because there are no test files, so the regression ships without notice.
input.severity_reason: This is missing test coverage, not wrong behavior in the code now. encrypt and decrypt are not called anywhere else in the repository. Leaving authenticated-encryption code untested is still a significant reliability and security-maintenance risk, so Medium fits better than the High the review assigned.
